title: loop checkpoint: pre-spawn checkpoint write, counters carried verbatim on 'reset', git-log check before discarding work (R7)
description: Deep-review sweep #2 (2026-07-06) MEDIUM finding R7 (F3+F5, adversarially confirmed). (a) The documented cadence (loop.md:63-66, SKILL.md:551-553) writes nothing between the fetch-phase checkpoint and the Developer's return — the longest phase, where test:/impl commits land. A mid-spawn crash resumes as in_progress+'fetch' → resumePoint returns 'reset' ('no durable work landed', src/loop-checkpoint.js:40,162-168), flipping the ticket to todo and re-driving it over already-landed commits (duplicate commits, broken red-run TDD evidence). (b) All three 'reset' returns (loop-checkpoint.js:142-147,154-159,162-168) omit iteration/completed_this_run/run_started_at — the very counters 'none'/'resume' carry verbatim to prevent silent zeroing — so a crash on a reset branch restarts the maxIterations and Gate-5 consolidation ceilings. Full context: synthesis §R7.
acceptance_criteria: loop.md and both SKILL.md copies add a mandatory checkpoint write immediately BEFORE the Developer spawn (phase 'test' for tdd / 'impl' otherwise), so a mid-spawn crash resumes at a post-fetch phase instead of falsely resetting.

All three 'reset' results in src/loop-checkpoint.js carry iteration, completed_this_run, and run_started_at verbatim from loop_state — red-first spec proving today's counter loss on a reset branch, then green.

The documented reset protocol requires checking git log for commits referencing the ticket key before discarding work; when such commits exist the protocol routes to resume/surface instead of silent reset (documented in loop.md + SKILL.md; helper code if implemented gets specs).
resumePoint's phase semantics after the new cadence are covered: in_progress at phase 'test'/'impl' with landed commits resumes rather than resets.
